title: Internal coinduction along a prime-power coefficient quotient
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $1\leq s\leq r$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$ and $\Lambda_s=\mathbf Z/\ell^s\mathbf Z$, a $\Lambda$-algebra through the quotient map. Let $X$ be a scheme and use the derived categories of module sheaves over the constant rings $\Lambda_X$, $\Lambda_{s,X}$ on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], restriction of scalars along $\Lambda_X\to\Lambda_{s,X}$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ put $K_s=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(\Lambda_{s,X},K)\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda_s)$. For every $M\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda_s)$ there is an isomorphism $$R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(M,K)\cong R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_s}(M,K_s)$$ in $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, natural in $M$ and $K$, where $M$ on the left and the right-hand side are viewed as $\Lambda$-complexes by restriction of scalars. It is the internal derived form of the restriction--coinduction adjunction: a local section $\phi:M\to K_s$ is sent to its composite with evaluation at $1\in\Lambda_s$, $K_s\to K$. No potentiality, constructibility or bound beyond $D^+$ is assumed. The two internal Hom objects need not lie in $D^+$ when $M$ is unbounded above; the asserted comparison is in the unbounded ambient category.

proof.text: Write $R=\Lambda_X$, $S=\Lambda_{s,X}$ and $U$ for scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. It is exact: kernels and the sheafified cokernels retain the same underlying abelian sheaves. For an $R$-module sheaf $F$ put $C(F)=\mathcal Hom_R(S,F)$, using [def-pur-sheaf-hom], with $S$-action $(a\phi)(b)=\phi(ab)$ on every localized site. Associativity, the unit law and distributivity follow respectively from $(ab)c=a(bc)$, $1b=b$ and distributivity in $S$; the formulas commute with restriction. Evaluation $e_F:C(F)\to F$, $e_F(\phi)=\phi(1)$, is $R$-linear since $\phi(q(r))=r\phi(1)$ for the ring map $q:R\to S$. Postcomposition defines $C$ on maps; it is additive.

source.place: Tag 04TT (section-internal-hom), Lemma 03EM (lemma-internal-hom); explicit evaluation formulas, analogous to Modules Tag 0A6F (lemma-adjoint-tensor-restrict), proved here on localized sites

proof.text: For an $S$-module sheaf $N$, the maps $\psi\mapsto e_F\psi$ and $f\mapsto\widehat f$, where $\widehat f(n)(b)=f(bn)$, identify $S$-linear maps $N\to C(F)$ with $R$-linear maps $UN\to F$. Indeed $\widehat f(an)(b)=f(ban)=(a\widehat f(n))(b)$, $e_F\widehat f(n)=f(n)$, and $\widehat{e_F\psi}(n)(b)=\psi(bn)(1)=(b\psi(n))(1)=\psi(n)(b)$. Additivity and $R$-linearity follow by distributing $b$ and using $q(r)n=rn$. The same formulas on each localized site, compatible with restriction, give an isomorphism of sheaves $\mathcal Hom_R(UN,F)\cong U\mathcal Hom_S(N,C(F))$ by [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Precomposition in $N$ and postcomposition in $F$ commute with the formulas. In particular $U\dashv C$.

source.place: Tag 04TT (section-internal-hom), Lemma 03EM (lemma-internal-hom); explicit evaluation formulas, analogous to Modules Tag 0A6F (lemma-adjoint-tensor-restrict), proved here on localized sites

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives, lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], choose a bounded-below K-injective complex $I$ of injective $R$-module sheaves representing $K$. Apply $C$ termwise, writing $J=C(I)$. Step 2 and exactness of $U$ allow [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] to show that $J$ is K-injective as an $S$-complex. Its terms vanish below the same lower bound as $I$. By [def-pur-hom-complex], $UJ=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(S[0],I)$, so [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] identifies $UJ$ with $R\mathcal Hom_R(S,K)$. Thus $J$ gives precisely this derived internal Hom its natural $S$-action, and defines the object $K_s\in D^+(S)$ of the statement. In particular no injectivity of $UJ$ as an $R$-complex is asserted or needed.

Choose any cochain representative $A$ of $M$ over $S$. Apply the sheaf isomorphism of Step 2 to $N=A^p$, $F=I^{p+n}$ for every $p,n$, and take the products in [def-pur-hom-complex]. This gives $\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(UA,I)\cong U\mathcal Hom_S^\bullet(A,J)$. The map from right to left sends $\psi^p$ to $e_I\psi^p$; its inverse sends $f^p$ to $(a\mapsto(b\mapsto f^p(ba)))$. It commutes with the differential: evaluation at $1$ sends $d_J\psi-(-1)^n\psi d_A$ to $d_I(e_I\psi)-(-1)^n(e_I\psi)d_A$, since $e_I d_J=d_I e_I$ by postcomposition. The inverse consequently also commutes with the differential. Products are taken sectionwise, and restriction preserves the displayed formulas, so this is an isomorphism of complexes of sheaves, not only a bijection of global morphisms.

Localize the chain isomorphism of Step 4. The K-injectivity of $I$ over $R$ and $J$ over $S$ from Step 3 identifies the two complexes with $R\mathcal Hom_R(UM,K)$ and $U R\mathcal Hom_S(M,K_s)$ by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Scalar restriction preserves quasi-isomorphisms because it is exact (Step 1). The formulas commute with maps of $A$ and $I$. Changing representatives or K-injective resolutions therefore gives the same derived comparison: the representative-change maps become isomorphisms by [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined], and their naturality squares already commute before localization. The resulting isomorphism is natural in both derived variables. Its inverse orientation is the comparison described in the statement, induced by evaluation at $1$. Only $J$ is asserted bounded below; no lower bound on the two Hom complexes is used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q42-e9a75bc5d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item and its source. Source: ILO Gabber XVII Prop. 6.2.1.1 (printed p. 294) prints the comparison 'dans D+(X_et,Λ)' for M in D+. That label is false. Counterexample I checked: X = Spec k̄, r = s = 1, K = F_ℓ[0], M = ⊕_{n≥0} F_ℓ[-n]; then RHom(M,K) has H^{-n} = F_ℓ for every n ≥ 0. The delivery changes the ambient category from D+ to D only and keeps every hypothesis and K_s in D+. The report names the change. The only citer, lem-per-gabber-local-duality-general step 4, gets its bounds from D_{K_1} and still holds. Step checks: U is exact; C = Hom_R(S,-) with its S-action and R-linear evaluation; I re-derived the U ⊣ C formulas and both inverse identities. The bounded-below injective K-injective I comes from 013K/070J. Stacks 08BJ (derived.tex:9857) has the right orientation (C is right adjoint to the exact U), so J = C(I) is S-K-injective and UJ = Hom^•(S[0],I). The degreewise products agree with the differential because e_I d_J = d_I e_I. Stacks 0A95 (sites-cohomology.tex:8754) gives independence of representatives and naturality. Duplicates: def-sfb-modobj-restrict-coextend-adjunction is the module-object version of Step 2 and does not apply directly to Mod(R_X), so the inline elementary step is fine. lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction is scalar extension, not coinduction. lem-per-potential-hom-coefficient-restriction is the pinning half of 6.2.1.1. I accept all four declared tool_uses as generic homological tools (enough injectives, D+ injective representative, 08BJ, 0A95). Edge cases s = r, X empty, M = 0 and non-flat r > s are fine. No SGA source is used, no new nodes are created and no fixes were written. Maintainer: please record the ILO 6.2.1.1 D+ → D source error in HUMAN.md.
